problem:
A rectangular plate of mass $M$ occupies the region
$D={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 1}.$
The mass density at each point is proportional to the square of its distance from the $x$-axis. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $y=2.$

activity_context.topic_title: Moments of Inertia of Laminas About Other Axes

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/b48e086ae0e94589d557eceb25b50af9deffdec442cfb7a4e559577bce899c40.png)

A triangular plate with mass $M$ occupies the region $D$ enclosed between the $x$-axis and the lines $x=1$ and $y=2x.$
The mass density at each point is proportional to its distance from the $x$-axis. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $x=-2.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 2x},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/f040a5500a1415b8617300f34074bb16d895889354ed7e722dbd668a233daebb.png)

Also, the distance between a point and the line $x=-2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-(-2)|=|x+2|.
$$

Next, the mass density can be written as $\lambda (x,y)=k|y|=ky,$ where $k$ is a constant of proportionality. We can find the value of $k$ by integrating the mass density function over the plate.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2x}ky\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{2x}y\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{1}2{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =k\cdot {[\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}k.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\lambda (x,y)=ky=\frac{3M}{2}y.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=-2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2x}\frac{3M}{2}y\,|x+2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2x}\frac{3M}{2}y(x+2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(x+2)^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{2x}y\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(x+2)^{2}{[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}2{x}^{2}(x+2)^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}2{x}^{4}+8{x}^{3}+8{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{[\frac{2}{5}{x}^{5}+2{x}^{4}+\frac{8}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}[\frac{2}{5}+2+\frac{8}{3}-0] \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}[\frac{76}{15}] \\  & =\frac{38M}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
